title: Early Learning Shapes Later Directions Of Representation Change In Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.36081v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Representations continually change as a network learns new tasks. We ask whether early representational changes naturally form a geometric structure that continues to shape later learning. We identify a low-dimensional subspace of early representation drift, which we call a scaffold, and test whether it is reused across subsequent tasks. Across four pretrained visual encoders and two datasets, later representational changes consistently favor this early-defined subspace over matched random alternatives. This reuse is history-dependent: when networks experience different early tasks but identical later training inputs, each network preferentially reuses the scaffold induced by its own learning history. The same preference appears in individual optimizer updates, even though the network's dominant local response directions shift away from the original scaffold. translated_title: 持续学习中早期学习塑造后续表征变化的方向
translated_abstract: 随着网络学习新任务，其表征会不断变化。我们探究早期的表征变化是否会自然形成一个持续影响后续学习的几何结构。我们识别出早期表征漂移的一个低维子空间，称之为“脚手架”（scaffold），并检验它在后续任务中是否被重复使用。在四个预训练视觉编码器和两个数据集上，后续的表征变化始终偏向这一早期定义的子空间，而非与之匹配的随机替代方案。这种复用依赖于历史：当网络经历不同的早期任务但接受完全相同的后续训练输入时，每个网络都会优先复用由其自身学习历史所诱导的脚手架。同样的偏好在单个优化器更新中也存在，尽管网络的主导局部响应方向已偏离原始脚手架。最后，将运动约束在脚手架内会减慢新任务的习得……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文发现持续学习中早期的表征变化会形成一个低维“脚手架”子空间，后续任务乃至单个优化器更新都会以依赖学习历史的方式优先复用这一子空间。
en_tdlr: In continual learning, early representational changes form a low-dimensional "scaffold" subspace that later tasks—and even individual optimizer updates—preferentially reuse in a history-dependent manner.
